chunks: And through this chain of narrators from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari that he said: I heard Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) say:

Among the sins that are not forgiven is the saying of a man: 'If only I were not punished except for this [one sin].' I said to myself: 'This is indeed subtle; it is appropriate for a man to scrutinize his affairs and his self in everything.' Then Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) turned to me and said: 'O Abu Hashim, you are right. Hold fast to what your self suggested to you, for polytheism among people is more concealed than the creeping of a gnat on a smooth stone on a dark night, or on a black floor.'

key_terms.دُبِيبِ الذَّرِّ: The creeping of a gnat/small insect

ai.seo_question: What is the subtle sin of assuming other sins are forgiven while focusing on one?
ai.summary: Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.) warns against the subtle spiritual danger of fixating on a single major sin while neglecting the accumulation of minor transgressions, a state of heedlessness that can mask underlying polytheism (shirk). He illustrates the extreme difficulty of detecting this hidden shirk by comparing it to a gnat crawling on a smooth stone in the dark, emphasizing the need for rigorous self-accountability (muhasabah) in Shia spiritual practice. This hadith underscores the comprehensive nature of sin, where minor neglects can erode the foundation of faith just as significantly as major offenses.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 176 - It is narrated through the same chain of narrators from Abu Hashim Ja’fari that he said: I heard Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) say:

Among the sins that would not be forgiven is when a person says: If only I were not punished, except for this sin! I said to myself: This matter is very complicated and it is best for man to be wary of his self in his internal matters in everything. At that moment the Imam glanced at me and said: O Abdul Hashim, you thought right. You must be careful of every incident and matter, because polytheism in people is more concealed than the movement of the ant on a smooth stone on a dark night or on the surface of black floor.
